title: Fleet order staggering playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick working playbook for staggering GPU orders across regions and SKUs to smooth lead-time variability, reduce shipment landing spikes, and preserve a 6–10 week effective runway for serving growth. This is an ops-oriented spreadsheet-style plan (not final procurement contract).

High-level goals:
- Avoid >25% cluster growth in any single week for us-east-1 or eu-west-1 to reduce on-call and deployment risk.
- Maintain >=8 weeks of cold-runway (unprovisioned capacity) at target 70% util for hosted API.
- Reduce capital burn spikes by smoothing purchase cadence (goal: monthly cadence with small weekly shipments where possible).

Immediate constraints / assumptions:
- Current committed fleet (as of inventory snapshot 2024-09-01): 5k A100-80GB equiv units (mix across regions), 1.8k H100 equiv, 400 LlamaSrv-optimized low-memory units.
- Supplier lead times (observed): Asia vendors: 18–26 weeks; US vendors: 12–18 weeks; EU vendors: 16–22 weeks. Lead-time variance +/- 4 weeks historically.
- Customs / import variability: add 2–6 business days for US, 7–14 for EU, 10–21 for APAC depending on carrier.
- Target SKU mix for next 9 months: 60% H100-class for peak throughput, 30% A100-style for mixed workloads, 10% cost-optimized small SKUs for embedding-heavy jobs.

Staggering rules (decision heuristics):
1) Bucket orders into three sizes: small (<=48 units), medium (49–320), large (>320). Prefer small/medium for APAC shipments to avoid port congestion windows.
2) For a given region, never schedule >2 large shipments within a rolling 12-week window.
3) If lead-time variance is > +/- 3 weeks for a vendor, split the order across two vendors and align second tranche for +6 weeks after first arrival.
4) Prioritize mixed-SKU containers (H100 + A100) when possible to reduce single-SKU backlogs in regional racks.
5) Hold 5% of monthly capex as emergency soft-commit (can be converted to spot-backed burst capacity).

Planned order pipeline (sheet rows emulated):
- Row format: [order_id | sku | qty | region | vendor | PO_date | est_ship_window | est_arrival_range | notes]
- O-2024-091: H100-96q | 120 | us-east-1 | VendorA | 2024-09-15 | 12–16 wks | 2025-01-01 — 2025-02-15 | split across 2 containers, stagger 3wk
- O-2024-092: A100-80 | 240 | eu-west-1 | VendorB | 2024-09-20 | 16–20 wks | 2025-01-15 — 2025-03-05 | medium order, customs buffer +10d
- O-2024-093: H100-96q | 48 | ap-northeast-1 | VendorC | 2024-09-22 | 20–26 wks | 2025-02-01 — 2025-04-15 | small local batch to reduce lead variance
- O-2024-094: Opt-SKU-30 | 120 | global-bunk | VendorD | 2024-09-25 | 14–18 wks | 2025-01-25 — 2025-03-15 | cost-optimized units allocated to embeddings routes

Simple rolling capacity forecast (notes, not full table):
- Baseline growth assumption: +7% monthly prod token volume -> effective GPU demand +6% month-over-month.
- With current pipeline, effective usable capacity (post-quantization/infra overhead) projected to be: 4% deficit at end of Q4 2024, 9% deficit by mid-Feb 2025 unless we accelerate any US vendors.
- If VendorA shortens shipments by average 2 weeks, deficit reduced to ~1% in Feb 2025.

Risk register (short bullets):
- Supplier delay (major): impact = regional cold-runway loss -> mitigation = pull-forward smaller PO from alternate vendor (action: procurement to keep 2 active quotes per SKU).
- Container consolidation slowdown at LA port: impact = batch arrival spike -> mitigation = split shipments, favor air-freight for urgent tranches (cost delta noted below).
- SKU obsolescence / firmware compatibility: impact = slower rack bring-up -> mitigation = pre-cert small sample rack for each new SKU (reserve 8 units for early testing).

Cost tradeoffs (back-of-envelope):
- Air-freight for urgent 24-unit tranche: +18–28% to unit landed cost vs sea for APAC -> justified if avoids >3-week capacity gap.
- Splitting across vendors increases procurement overhead (~1.5% extra admin) but reduces single-point-of-failure risk.

Operational checklist before PO sign (TODOs):
- [ ] Confirm acceptance test cases with SRE + bench team (bench PR: ops/bench#56).
- [ ] Attach firmware and BIOS compatibility matrix to PO (owner: Tom).
- [ ] Reserve customs broker slot and temporary rack space in region (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Add fallback budget line to finance for +12% overspend in Q1 if air freight used.

Unresolved questions / open decisions:
- Q1 scaling target: should we accept higher short-term burn (air freight) to secure more aggressive H100 mix? Product requests more latency headroom for new features; need quick decision from product infra by 2024-10-10.
- VendorC minimal order sizes are sticky — can procurement negotiate staggered partials? (Procurement to escalate, task: JIRA-INFRA-4123).

Slack / reference threads:
- #infra-procurement: convo link (Slack timestamp 2024-09-10 14:33) — note: vendorA offered a rolling-delivery discount if >200 units.
- Internal bench results: bench/2024-q3-h100-latency.md (attached in confluence link above).

Quick simulation snippet (text):
- If we take O-2024-091 + O-2024-092 on current lead times, arrival distribution by week shows two small spikes Jan-Feb 2025. Smoothing option: move 40% of O-2024-092 to VendorE with 12–14wk lead -> reduces spike amplitude by ~40% but increases landed cost ~6%.

Next steps (short):
- Procurement: confirm 2nd vendor quotes for O-2024-092 by 2024-09-30.
- Finance: prepare contingency approval for air-freight up to $1.2M by 2024-10-07.
- SRE / Bench: run compatibility tests on 8 vendor-sample units within 7 days of arrival.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc lightweight; mirror to confluence if we decide a canonical ops playbook.
- Remember to track landed vs estimated arrival and keep weekly quick standup with procurement until all current POs are delivered.

Week | Region | Expected arrivals | SKU mix | Contingency
2025-01-01 | us-east-1 | 120 | H100 100% | +air freight option on 2/3 tranche
2025-01-15 | eu-west-1 | 120 | A100 80% / H100 20% | customs buffer 10d
2025-02-10 | ap-northeast-1 | 48 | H100 100% | hold 8 units for bench

(End of draft)
